info.description:
HTTP API for Claude Code, Goose, and Aider.

https://github.com/coder/agentapi
info.title: AgentAPI

delete.description: Removes the session cookie. Reachable without credentials.

schema.description: The session cookie (POST) or its removal (DELETE).

get.description: Reports whether the server requires an API token and whether this request is authenticated. Reachable without credentials.

schema.description: The session cookie (POST) or its removal (DELETE).

post.description: Requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and sets an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict session cookie that authenticates later requests, including EventSource and image requests that can't send headers. The cookie holds a value derived from the token, not the token itself, so changing the token signs every browser out. Without --api-token it sets nothing.

schema.description: The session cookie (POST) or its removal (DELETE).

post.description: Has the agent summarize the conversation so far to free its context window (Codex: in a turn of its own; Pi: answered once done). Native transport only, for agents with the compact capability. Messages sent meanwhile wait in the queue. Returns 409 while the agent works on a turn or compacts, and when it refuses (Pi with nothing to compact yet).

get.description: Returns what the session the agent has open spent, its subagents included, and its model calls one by one, read from the agent's logs: the tokens of each call priced at the model providers' list prices (the API-equivalent cost, which a subscription doesn't charge), or at Pi's own prices for Pi. A model without a known price counts its tokens and no cost; --prices adds prices. For Claude Code, what it counted but didn't log call by call (compacting the context) comes as unitemized calls. Native transport of Claude Code, Codex and Pi only.

The events are sent as Server-Sent Events (SSE). Initially, the endpoint returns a list of events needed to reconstruct the current state of the conversation and the agent's status. After that, it only returns events that have occurred since the last event was sent.

The server ends the stream when the client falls too far behind, when the conversation changes in a way updates can't express (a message was taken back), which gives it a new epoch, and when a long session is opened (POST /sessions/{id}/resume). Reconnect to get the state again: with sync, the old epoch gets the full state.

Note: When an agent is running, the last message in the conversation history is updated frequently, and the endpoint sends a new message update event each time.

post.description: Stops the turn the agent is working on. Native transport only, for agents with the interrupt capability.

delete.description: Forgets the turn a usage limit stopped, with its scheduled continuation, so the queued messages go out as soon as the agent can take them. Native transport only; returns 409 when no turn stopped on a limit.
Cancels the continuation POST /limit/continue or --auto-continue scheduled. The queued messages still wait until the limit resets. Native transport only; returns 409 when no turn stopped on a limit.

post.description: Continues the turn a usage limit stopped (`limit_stop` in GET /status) with a message asking the agent to go on: now, or once the limit resets (`at: reset`, which needs the reset time). While a continuation is scheduled the queued messages wait for it; sending a message yourself cancels it. Native transport only; returns 409 when no turn stopped on a limit.

While `login_required` is reported in GET /status, checks again now whether the user logged in (AgentAPI also checks every few seconds while the agent waits at startup). If the agent lost its login while running, it is restarted and resumes its session. Native transport only; returns 409 if no login is needed.

get.description:
Returns the complete MCP server configuration used by the running agent.

Supported agents and files:

- **Claude:** project-scoped `.mcp.json` in the agent working directory (`mcpServers` object).
- **Codex:** `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml`, falling back to `~/.codex/config.toml` (`[mcp_servers.*]` tables).
- **Pi:** user-level `$PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/mcp.json`, falling back to `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json` (`mcpServers` object).

Server values are agent-native and passed through without transport-specific validation. The response can contain environment values or HTTP headers, so treat it as sensitive. Other agent types return `404`.

value.detail: MCP config management is not supported for this agent type
value.title: Not Found

put.description:
Replaces the agent's **complete** MCP server map while preserving unrelated config-file content.

Important behavior:

- Servers omitted from `servers` are removed; send `{"servers": {}}` to clear all MCP servers.
- Values use the target agent's native format and are not validated by AgentAPI.
- Without `restart=true`, the new configuration is loaded by the next agent session.
- With `restart=true`, AgentAPI replaces the agent process immediately. AgentAPI and its HTTP/SSE endpoints stay online. A PTY agent starts over with an empty conversation; a native agent resumes its session, so the conversation stays (409 while it works on a turn).
- Restart is unavailable in ACP, schema-only, and other server modes without a process supervisor; those requests return `400`.
- A missing or structurally invalid request body returns `422`.
- Claude, Codex and Pi are supported; other agent types return `404`.

parameters.description: Restart the agent after writing the config so changes apply immediately; AgentAPI stays online. A PTY agent's conversation is reset; a native agent resumes its session (409 while it works on a turn). Supported for supervised PTY sessions and the native transport.

get.description: Returns a list of rich structured messages. Each message contains structured content blocks (text, thinking, tool_use, tool_result), model information, and token usage data. With the PTY transport they are parsed from the session log of agents that have one (claude, codex and pi); with the native transport they come from the agent's protocol.

Lists the sessions the agent had in the working directory, read from its session logs (Claude Code's projects directory, Codex's sessions, Pi's session directory), the latest first, with the one it has open. Sessions in which the user sent nothing are left out. Native transport of Claude Code, Codex and Pi only.

post.description: Restarts the agent on one of its sessions from GET /sessions, or with `fork` on a copy of it under a new id, and replaces the conversation with that session's, read from its log. The queue and the open requests are cleared, as on a restart. Native transport of Claude Code, Codex and Pi only; returns 404 for a session the agent has no log of here, and 409 while the agent works on a turn or compacts its context (nothing changes then) or another restart is under way.

get.description: Returns the agent's permission mode, model and reasoning effort, and the values they can take. The current settings are also part of GET /status and `status_change` events. Native transport only, for agents with the settings capability; returns 409 while the agent restarts or waits for a login.

put.description: Changes the settings that are set in the body and leaves the others: `permission_mode` (bypass, auto, ask or plan, as the agent offers), `model` (one of the model ids GET /settings lists) and `effort` (one of the model's efforts). A change made during a turn may apply from the next one (Codex). The agent that replaces this one after a restart, a new login or an AgentAPI restart (with --state-db) gets the chosen settings too. Native transport only; returns 400 for a value a setting can't take and 409 while the agent restarts or waits for a login.

get.description: Returns the conversation's tasks: each message of the user's and the agent's turn on it, until the agent is done (stable again, with no request or terminal dialog open). Messages the user adds while a task runs belong to it (steered). A task is running, completed, failed (the agent reported an error or exited) or limited (a usage limit stopped it). /events sends task_update when one starts or changes.

Streams a shell in the agent's working directory, for a terminal emulator: `output` events carry what it writes (the first one the recent output), and an `exit` event ends the stream when the shell exits; a connection that falls too far behind ends without one, and connects again for the recent output. Connecting starts the shell if it doesn't run; it keeps running while nobody watches, and every connection shares it. Native transport only (on by default; --terminal=false turns it off).
